facts.statement: The genus contains only one known species, Mbiresaurus raathi, which is known from a nearly complete skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Mbiresaurus raathi, known from a nearly complete skeleton.

facts.statement: Mbiresaurus represents one of Africa's earliest known definitive dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Mbiresaurus represents one of Africa's earliest known definitive dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a mostly complete skeleton including a partial skull, jaws, vertebrae, ribs, girdles, and partial limbs.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a mostly complete, partially-articulated skeleton, including a partial skull and lower jaws, cervical, dorsal, sacral, and caudal vertebrae, fragments of ribs, partial pectoral and pelvic girdles, and partial forelimbs and hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses by Griffin et al. (2022) recovered Mbiresaurus as a basal member of Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Griffin et al. (2022) recovered Mbiresaurus as a basal member of Sauropodomorpha.

facts.statement: Mbiresaurus lived during the late Triassic, approximately 231 to 228 million years ago, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente entre 231 y 228 millones de años, en el Carniense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: The time range for Mbiresaurus is the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Pebbly Arkose Formation also contains fossils of Hyperodapedon, unnamed aetosaurs, herrerasaurids, and synapsids.
facts.quote: Other fossils belonging to Hyperodapedon, as well as unnamed aetosaurs, herrerasaurids, and synapsids (possible dicynodont and gomphodontosuchine traversodontid cynodont) have also been recovered from the formation.
